title: Critical Apparatus Encoding & TEI Apparatus Structures
query: How does the TEI P5 Critical Apparatus module (tei:app, lem, rdg) structure manuscript variants, and how can automated pipelines and AI assistants support apparatus construction and error detection?

results.title: Evaluating AI for the Digital Scholarly Edition
results.authors_venue_year: Evaluating AI for the Digital Scholarly EditionKM Penner - Artificial Intelligence for Bible Translation and …, 2026 - torrossa.comExplains the use of the TEI P5 Critical Apparatus module elements `<app>`, `<lem>`, and `<rdg>` with the `@wit` attribute to encode textual variants, contrasting the lemma text with alternative readings from different witnesses.AI Support for Apparatus: Evaluates the ability of AI chatbots to identify textual differences and encode them according to TEI standards, specifically using the `<app>`, `<lem>`, and `<rdg>` elements, as part of the scholarly workflow.Improving AI Accuracy: Demonstrates how detailed, explicit instructions in prompts significantly improve the performance of AI chatbots in encoding transcriptions into the TEI P5 XML format, which is crucial for apparatus construction.Save Cite Related articles All 2 versions

results.title: The Scholarly Edition Workflow: Tradition Meets Technology
results.authors_venue_year: The Scholarly Edition Workflow: Tradition Meets TechnologyKM Penner - Artificial Intelligence for Bible Translation and …, 2026 - books.google.comExplains the use of the `<app>`, `<lem>`, and `<rdg>` elements by detailing a task where chatbots were instructed to identify textual differences among multiple versions and encode these variants using these specific TEI elements with appropriate `@wit` attributes.AI for TEI Encoding: Evaluates the capability of AI chatbots to automate tasks such as transcribing text from manuscript images and encoding it into the TEI P5 standard, including specific elements for page breaks, columns, and line breaks.AI Limitations in Variant Detection: Demonstrates the limitations of current AI models (Claude 3.5 Haiku, Gemini 1.5 Flash, and OpenAI GPT 4o mini) in accurately detecting and encoding textual variants into TEI, concluding that they failed to produce usable TEI encoding for this specific task.Save Cite Related articles  Found early results.
